newsitem.title: SENEGAL: Senegal to sell hotels, vegetable oil processor.
newsitem.headline: Senegal to sell hotels, vegetable oil processor.

text.p: Senegal is looking for buyers for its stake in two hotels and a vegetable oil processing company in the latest round of privatisations, officials said on Wednesday.

The privatisation committee of the coastal West African state said the luxury Hotel Meridien President in the capital Dakar would be sold, along with the state's 32.28 percent stake in the SPHU-Teranga hotel.
Management of the Hotel Meridien President is already in the private hands of the Meridien group.
"The privatisation will be done in the form of a sale of the real estate," Serigne Ahmadou Kamara, head of the privatisation committee told Reuters.
The SPHU-Teranga hotel, 44 percent owned by France's Accor, recorded a loss of 92 million CFA francs in 1995.

A 51 percent stake in vegetable oil processing company SONACOS is being offered for the second time. Since the government first said it wanted to sell its shares last year, only very low offers have been received.
Senegal, an exporter of fish, phosphates and groundnuts as well as a tourist destination, has been encouraged by foreign donors to sell off its state enterprises.
